info.bio: Inspiral Carpets es un grupo de indie británico formado en Oldham (Inglaterra) en el año 1986 por Graham Lambert, convirtiéndose, tras The Stone Roses y Happy Mondays, en el grupo más popular de la escena bautizada como Madchester. Su sonido está basado en el órgano entre melódico y psicodélico de Clint Boon, y en las guitarras propias del sonido garage, además de un sonido de bajo muy apreciable..., mientras que su nombre psicodélicamente had-hoc al tema de su revival de los 60's, fue debido a una tienda de alfombras cerca de Oldham.

scenes.name: Psicodelia británica de los noventa
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La edad de oro de la psicodelia británica no fueron los sesenta sino los noventa: las raves crean una demanda inagotable de música inducida por (o para) las drogas. La versión pop (Telescopes, Inspiral Carpets, Verve, Sundial, Auteurs, Kula Shaker), las más sofisticadas (Curve, Cranberries, Rollerskate Skinny, Beta Band, dEUS, Gorky's Zygotic Mynci), el space-rock libre (Porcupine Tree, Terminal Cheesecake, Heads), los últimos shoegazers (Ride, Swervedriver, Spectrum y E.A.R. de Sonic Boom, Spiritualized de Jason Pierce, Flying Saucer Attack, encuentro de shoegazing y ambient) y el dream-pop (Lush, Pale Saints, Slowdive, Catherine Wheel, Bark Psychosis).

scenes.name: Mánchester: la Haçienda y Madchester
scenes.book: Techno Rebels: The Renegades of Electronic Funk
scenes.author: Dan Sicko
scenes.desc: En 1988, fuera del círculo de Rhythm King, había que ir a Mánchester para oír discos de Detroit: en la Haçienda (financiada por New Order) Mike Pickering, criado en el soul, pinchaba «Goodbye Kiss», «Groovin’ without a Doubt» o «Triangle of Love» antes que nadie en Londres, donde en el Spectrum no sonaban. La ciudad de los Smiths, The Fall y New Order unió el indie al acid house con los Happy Mondays, los Stone Roses e Inspiral Carpets, un puente hacia 808 State y A Guy Called Gerald.

podcast.title: Noel Gallagher's Roadie Gig (1988)
podcast.body: Before joining Oasis, Noel Gallagher worked as a roadie for the band Inspiral Carpets around 1988. This job offered him early exposure to the practicalities of touring and the music industry. "Noel eventually got a job as a roadie with the Inspiral Carpets."

podcast.title: Conflict with Noel Gallagher
podcast.body: Noel Gallagher, who later rose to fame with Oasis, had a past "fall out with Sean" (presumably Shaun Ryder, or a member of Inspiral Carpets named Sean) because "Sean had some words in his spirals," indicating a disagreement or conflict involving the band. "He'd fallen out with Sean because Sean had some words in his spirals."

podcast.title: Distinctive Sound
podcast.body: The band was known for having a distinct 1960s vibe in their music, which was significantly influenced by their use of a Farfisa organ. "And same thing, I guess, with the carpets, they obviously had the Farrifisa organ, and they had more of a sixties vibe."

podcast.title: Noel Gallagher's Roadie Role
podcast.body: Noel Gallagher, who would later form Oasis, was a roadie for Inspiral Carpets, transporting their guitars and amps. This period foreshadowed his significant impact on the music scene. "it would be up to one of their roadies, the guy who told of their guitars and amps from place to place who would help change everything."

podcast.title: Noel Gallagher's Roadie Work
podcast.body: Noel Gallagher worked as a roadie for Inspiral Carpets, using his downtime to write songs and accumulate home demos by September 1989. He also played the opening chords of what would become Oasis' "Live Forever" repeatedly during soundchecking duties for the band. "Noel, who was working as a roadie for Inspiral Carpets, spent his downtime writing songs."

xref.title: Meeting Graham Lambert at Stone Roses Show (1988)
xref.body: In 1988, Noel Gallagher met Graham Lambert, the guitarist for the Inspiral Carpets, at a Stone Roses concert. This meeting sparked a friendship and his initial connection to the Inspiral Carpets. "Then in 1988 he met Graham Lambert at a stone rosa show."

xref.title: Roadie for Inspiral Carpets (1988)
xref.body: By 1988, after moving out of his family home, Noel Gallagher secured a job as a roadie for the band Inspiral Carpets. This experience gave him insight into the music industry before he joined Liam's band, Rain, which later became Oasis. "Noel eventually got a job as a roadie with the Inspiral Carpets."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Oasis at War: Part 1

xref.title: Noel Gallagher's "Coup d'Etat" (Spring 1993)
xref.body: In the spring of 1993, after being fired from his job as a guitar roadie with the Inspiral Carpets and left with only £2,000 in severance pay, Noel Gallagher was determined to forge a proper music career. While impressed by his younger brother Liam's band, he offered to join on the strict condition, effectively a "coup d'etat," that he be "in charge of everything" within the group. "I will join your group, he said, but you have to let me be in charge of everything."

xref.body: Craig Gill, a member of Inspiral Carpets, died by suicide on November 22, 2016. "November 22nd, Craig Gillib, Inspiral Carpets, Suicide."

xref.title: Ambition to Surpass Inspiral Carpets
xref.body: Keyboardist Clint Boon of the Inspiral Carpets observed that Noel Gallagher "was always writing songs" and "had a swagger," suggesting his potential. Noel himself, watching from the wings, thought, "I can do better than this," indicating his strong ambition to transcend his roadie role and outperform the band he was working for. "Watching them from the wings, he said, I thought, I can do better than this."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Departure from Inspiral Carpets
xref.body: Steve Holt, who was the "localist" for the Inspiral Carpets, left the band. His departure prompted Noel Gallagher to audition for the vacant position, although Gallagher was ultimately unsuccessful in securing the role. "Localist Steve Holt was leaving the band."

xref.title: Drug-Hiding Duty
xref.body: Among his roadie responsibilities, Noel Gallagher was tasked with hiding the Inspiral Carpets' drugs in their road cases. "And he was also in charge of hiding the band's drugs in their road cases."

xref.body: By 1988, Noel was living independently and eventually secured a job as a roadie for the band Inspiral Carpets, before joining Liam's band, Rain. "Noel eventually got a job as a roadie with the Inspiral Carpets."

xref.title: Early Interactions with Happy Mondays
xref.body: Gazz Wheeling and Kelly knew Noel Gallagher personally. Gazz recalls interviewing him "for a few drinks" in a downstairs area, noting a past conflict where Noel "had fallen out with Sean" (likely Shaun Ryder or a member of Inspiral Carpets) due to "words in his spirals." During this early interaction, Noel even offered to play drums for Happy Mondays if they ever needed someone. "He said, if you ever need anyone to do your drums, I'll do it."

xref.title: Failed Audition for Inspiral Carpets
xref.body: When Steve Holt, the localist for the Inspiral Carpets, left the band, Noel Gallagher saw an opportunity and auditioned for the gig. However, his audition was unsuccessful. "Noel thought I could do that and audition for the gig. That however didn't work out."

xref.title: Formation and First Gig
xref.body: Noel Gallagher, while working as a roadie for Inspiral Carpets, wrote songs in his downtime, amassing home demos by September 1989. In April 1990, the band Rain was co-founded by Paul "Bonehead" Arthurs and Chris Hutton, playing gigs at the Boardwalk in Manchester. Noel joined mid-1990, took over, and his younger brother became the singer. The group's first official gig as Oasis was on August 9, 1991. "The group's first gig as Oasis was on August 9, 1991."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In the Studio with Oasis

xref.title: Friendship with Mark Coyle
xref.body: As a roadie, Noel Gallagher became friends with Mark Coyle, the Inspiral Carpets' soundman. They spent hours discussing music, particularly The Beatles, and their songwriting ambitions. Mark Coyle also facilitated Noel's opportunities to practice on stage during downtime. "He also made friends with Mark Coil, the Carpets soundman. They spent hours talking about the Beatles and songwriting in their respective ambitions."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Guitar Roadie for Inspiral Carpets
xref.body: Despite his failed audition, Noel Gallagher's dedication as a "solid Carpets fan" led the band to offer him a job as a guitar roadie. He candidly admitted he had no prior knowledge of roadie work and learned as he went. "But because he was such a solid Carpets fan they gave him a job as a guitar roadie."

xref.title: Origin from "Rain" and Noel Gallagher's Takeover
xref.body: Noel Gallagher, formerly a roadie for Inspiral Carpets and later an employee in British Gas's parts department, launched a "coup d'état" on his younger brother Liam's band, then called "Rain." He renamed it Oasis and took over all songwriting responsibilities. "Nole Gallagher launched a coup d'état on his younger brother's band, which was called Rain. He renamed it Oasis and took over. Everything, all the songwriting."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt Rock: Chapter 12

xref.title: Recognized Noel Gallagher's Potential
xref.body: Clint Boon, the keyboardist for the Inspiral Carpets, observed that Noel Gallagher, then their guitar roadie, was "always writing songs" and possessed a "swagger." Boon noted that the band knew Gallagher's roadie role would not be permanent, recognizing his greater potential. "Clint Boone, the keyboardist for the Carpets, remembered Noel was always writing songs. Even then he had a swagger. We all knew he wasn't going to be a roadie forever."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Soundman for Inspiral Carpets
xref.body: Mark Coyle worked as the soundman for the Inspiral Carpets. He became friends with Noel Gallagher, the band's guitar roadie, and they spent many hours discussing The Beatles and songwriting. Coyle also facilitated Gallagher's ability to practice on stage. "He also made friends with Mark Coil, the Carpets soundman."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: We Are The Road Crew - A History of Roadies

xref.title: Taking Control of Rain (Later Oasis)
xref.body: In 1991, upon returning from an American tour with the Inspiral Carpets, Noel Gallagher learned his brother Liam had joined a band called Rain. Unimpressed, he rejected Liam's offer to manage them, instead demanding full control of the band and becoming its sole songwriter. The band accepted, and they were subsequently renamed Oasis. "I will take control of the band and become its only songwriter. Take it or leave it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: We Are The Road Crew - A History of Roadies

xref.title: UK Reunion Tour (2010s)
xref.body: Against initial odds, the Happy Mondays reunited for a series of shows across the UK, signaling a significant return for the band known for its Madchester era excesses. The tour included a stop at Brixton Academy where Inspiral Carpets opened. "But, against all odds, the Mondays came back together for a series of shows across the UK."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Stop Me If You've Heard This One Before

xref.title: World Tour with Inspiral Carpets
xref.body: For two years, Noel Gallagher toured the world with the Inspiral Carpets during what were described as some of the band's best years. In this role, he was responsible for looking after the guitars and gained invaluable experience in various aspects of life on the road, including customs, airports, hotels, crowd management, and the dynamics of a well-known band. "And for the next two years some of the best years of the Inspiral Carpets career. Noel toured the world with them looking after the guitars."
